readback.name: Poincare.GlobalParametrixAssembly.ambient_norm_le
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For every universe u, let M : Type u have a topology, an E3 charted-space structure, and the C-infinity IsManifold structure for the boundaryless closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3, at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat. Let A : AtlasData M, with finite extended charts C_j, open subordinate covering regions whose closures lie in their chart sources and have compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity p_j. No Hausdorff, CompactSpace, connectedness, metric, or flow hypothesis is explicitly assumed. Let alpha and T be arbitrary real parameters. Scalar alpha T is the original scalar-valued Y space, and Jet alpha T is the original Graph space over E3. Y fields are zero off the cylinder Icc 0 T times all of E3 and their norm is the sum of the value supremum and the alpha-Hoelder seminorm measured within that cylinder, with parabolic distance norm(x-y) + sqrt(abs(t-s)). Graph contains u,ut,du,ddu Y fields, zero initial u trace, genuine ordinary spatial derivative certificates u -> du -> ddu for times in Icc 0 T, and a within-Icc 0 T time derivative certificate u -> ut. Its norm is the sum of the four Y norms. Y_M A alpha T is the canonical submodule subtype of chart/component-indexed Scalar entries satisfying pointwise spatial support in coordSupport A j, symmetry in the two component indices, and the original partition-weighted overlap equation on genuine chart overlaps. Its norm is inherited from the existing finite Pi norm on those Scalar entries. SourceGraphs alpha T is the nine-component function space (Fin 3 times Fin 3) -> Jet alpha T with its existing finite Pi norm. Let S_j be any family of continuous real-linear maps Scalar alpha T -> Jet alpha T. Let B be any Transports A alpha T family, with B_ijcd : SourceGraphs alpha T ->L[R] Jet alpha T. The pinned localGraphs_j map sends f in Y_M to the family (a,b) |-> S_j(f.val(j,a,b)), using the same S_j on every source component. The actual pinned ambient continuous real-linear map has component ambient(f)_(i,c,d) = the finite sum over every source chart j of B_ijcd(localGraphs_j(f)). Its codomain is the original LocalProduct A (Jet alpha T), the finite Pi space of chart/component-indexed Graphs, before any codomain restriction. For every real CP and every real array CB_ijcd, assume CP >= 0, every CB_ijcd >= 0, and operator norm(B_ijcd) <= CB_ijcd for all chart indices i,j and component indices c,d. Assume also only the following support-restricted local solver estimate: for every j and every h in Scalar alpha T, if h(t,z) = 0 for every ambient product point whose spatial coordinate z is outside coordSupport A j, then norm(S_j h) <= CP * norm(h). The support premise is on the total scalar function and all times, rather than a restriction only to in-cylinder evaluation. No estimate norm(S_j) <= CP on the entire unrestricted Scalar space is assumed or concluded. Then the operator norm of the actual ambient map from Y_M to LocalProduct A (Jet alpha T) is at most CP times the finite total sum over i,j : Fin A.cover.chartCount and c,d : Fin 3 of CB_ijcd. The input operator norm uses the original submodule norm inherited from the finite Pi Scalar product; the output uses the original finite Pi norm of Graph entries. Each B norm likewise uses the existing nine-Graph Pi domain norm and original Graph sum norm. There is no replacement norm, added NormedSpace instance, or completeness premise. The sum and multiplication on the right are ordinary real arithmetic. The forcing domain restriction is essential: each f.val(j,a,b) has the stated spatial support because f is in Y_M, which permits applying the supported-input CP estimate componentwise. No assumption about transport chart values, a buffer family xi, symmetry preservation by B, or range membership is required in this norm statement. Alpha,T are unrestricted real parameters fixed before CP,CB, and the hypotheses may vary with those parameters; the lemma does not itself select CP or CB uniformly in T or supply a positive lifespan. It concludes a bound for the defined finite assembled continuous linear map, and does not construct the local solvers or transports, prove a codomain-restricted P equation, assert a small residual or contraction, or produce a global flow.
